newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma City blast trial date set for March 31.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma City blast trial date set for March 31.

text.p: Timothy McVeigh, one of the defendants in the Oklahoma City bombing case, will go on trial on March 31, a spokeswoman for the Justice Department said on Friday.
"We can confirm. The date is March 31," said spokeswoman Leesa Brown. McVeigh and co-defendant Terry Nichols will be tried separately.
McVeigh and Nichols are charged with the April 1995 truck-bombing that destroyed the Alfred P. Murrah federal building, resulting in the death of 168 people.
The two defendants have been present in court since Wednesday for a pre-trial hearing, but by court order will be tried separately with McVeigh going first.
The case has been moved to Denver because it was deemed nearly impossible for the two men to receive a fair hearing anywhere in Oklahoma.
Prosecutors have said they are prepared to go to trial very soon, while McVeigh's attorney Stephen Jones said on Thursday that he did not expect to be ready before May 1.
But when Jones was asked as he entered a closed-door hearing if he was happy about the date, he said: "You bet."

Patrick Ryan, U.S. Attorney for Oklahoma, also told reporters he was pleased. "We thought it was important to start before the second anniversary," Ryan told reporters, referring to the April 19 bombing date.
Victims and relatives of people who perished in the bombing have wanted the trial to begin as soon as possible.
